title: Longitudinal analysis of health-related quality of life after cardiac surgery/catheterization in the setting of congenital heart disease
summary:
Using an established and validated questionnaire, this study aims to assess health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in children with congenital heart disease and to follow its development over a period of twelve months after hospital admission for cardiac surgery or catheter-based intervention at the Department of Congenital Heart Defects.
The success of cardiac surgery or catheter-based interventions is commonly evaluated based on objective clinical outcomes such as survival, freedom from reintervention, or physical exercise capacity. However, these parameters provide only limited information on how children and their families experience the impact of the disease and necessary medical treatments in everyday life.
Congenital heart disease comprises a broad spectrum of conditions, ranging from defects that can be successfully treated through surgery or catheter-based interventions to complex conditions requiring lifelong medical care and follow-up. Therefore, this study aims to assess HRQoL in children with congenital heart disease and to investigate how HRQoL is associated with different aspects of disease complexity and treatment-related burden and how it changes over time.
The Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory™ Cardiac Module (PedsQL™ Cardiac Module) was specifically developed to assess HRQoL in children of different age groups with congenital heart disease. The questionnaire captures various dimensions of HRQoL and includes both self-reports by children and adolescents and proxy reports by parents or legal guardians.
Data collection will be performed electronically using the REDCap data capture system, allowing participation beyond the initial hospital stay. After the baseline assessment at study inclusion, follow-up assessments will be conducted after 3, 6, 9, and 12 months.
Patients will be enrolled over a period of five years. The collected data will contribute to a better understanding of which aspects of disease complexity and treatment-related burden are associated with differences in HRQoL among children with congenital heart disease. In the long term, the findings may support the development of needs-based follow-up care and support strategies for affected children and their families.

interventions.name: Survey at the time of admission before heart surgery/cardiac catheterisation with the Pediatric Quality of Life Inventory™ Cardiac Module and follow-up after 3, 6, 9 and 12 months.
Survey data from a healthy reference group are available.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Cardiac surgery/catheter in the context of a congenital heart disease
Exclusion criteria:
No cardiac surgery/catheter in the context of a congenital heart disease.
